statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-96231 (GHSA-2j93-m82w-73j2) is a .NET elevation of privilege issue in the runtime (Microsoft.NETCore.App, System.Private.CoreLib): on Unix, the named-mutex and shared-memory paths can be manipulated through insecure global directories, symbolic-link races and unsafe permission changes, so a local attacker can truncate or overwrite files, widen directory permissions or elevate privileges. Microsoft lists Linux and macOS as the affected platforms and the .NET 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2j93-m82w-73j2, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/479, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135707, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). The fix changes the Unix named-mutex code in System.Private.CoreLib and the shared-memory and mutex code of the runtime's platform layer in libcoreclr.so (dotnet/dotnet commit 46e12b57000895ce6d079112888fdc3e68198481 on release/10.0.1xx; the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.113 source tag, from which the 10.0.13 runtime and SDK 10.0.113 are built, contains it and v10.0.112 does not: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/46e12b57000895ce6d079112888fdc3e68198481). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's dotnet/dotnet source release, and each build's version is the .NET release it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: every build ships System.Private.CoreLib.dll and libcoreclr.so at its own .NET version, in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet10-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and in the runtime packs and runtime archives held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap (seven System.Private.CoreLib.dll and five libcoreclr.so copies per build and architecture); no copy from another .NET version is present. That version is 10.0.2 to 10.0.10 in the first nine builds and 10.0.13 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

Microsoft lists Linux and macOS as the affected platforms and the .NET 9.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 9.0.0 through 9.0.20 and fixed in 9.0.21 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2j93-m82w-73j2, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/479, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135707, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: every build ships System.Private.CoreLib.dll and libcoreclr.so at its own .NET version. The five System.Private.CoreLib.dll copies per build and architecture are in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet9-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap, and in that version's runtime pack and NativeAOT compiler pack held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap; the three libcoreclr.so copies are in the same two shared frameworks and the runtime pack. No copy from another .NET version is present. That version is 9.0.12 to 9.0.20 in the first eight builds and 9.0.21 or later from 9.0.21-r0 on (for example, System.Private.CoreLib.dll and libcoreclr.so carry version 9.0.2026.41315 in 9.0.20-r0 and 9.0.2126.50404 in 9.0.21-r0 on both architectures). The range ends at 9.0.21-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
